newsitem.title: FRANCE: French strikes disrupt public transport.
newsitem.headline: French strikes disrupt public transport.

text.p: A strike against French government austerity policies disrupted trains, buses, the Metro and flights on Thursday in the first big test of union disaffection since a crippling wave of unrest in late 1995.
The strike, mainly by five million public sector workers, was also due to keep schools closed, affect hospitals, and cut public services.
About one third of trains were running during the one-day stoppage, according to SNCF state railways. The Channel Tunnel link between Paris and London was unaffected.
Most lines on Paris's underground Metro railway were running as normal and 75 percent of buses in the capital were unaffected, limiting traffic jams around the city.
Strikes at airlines disrupted many domestic and international flights. Air France and Air Inter Europe were guaranteeing only 15 percent of flights.

An opinion poll in the daily Le Parisien showed 64 percent of French people backed the day of action by civil servants fighting job cuts planned as part of austerity to help France qualify for a single European currency from 1999.
